goal: Add opt-in hierarchy segment-depth bounding (--levels / --tree-depth) to recur tree while preserving --depth filesystem directory semantics and backwards compatibility.
invariants: Existing --depth <DEPTH> flag on recur tree MUST remain filesystem directory walk depth with zero behavioral change; tests/tree_configured_lanes.rs::configured_wildcard_scope_preserves_depth_and_separator_markers and julia-tests/runtests.tree.jl (including its @test_broken assertion on --depth 1) MUST continue to pass without Unexpected Pass or regression.
Hierarchy segment-depth bounding is strictly opt-in via a new flag (--levels <N> with visible alias --tree-depth <N>, where N >= 1 counts hierarchy segments beneath <BASE>).
When --levels / --tree-depth is omitted, recur tree text, --count, and --json outputs (name, children, path) are byte-for-byte unchanged for all existing inputs.
Configured wildcard scope patterns such as main.**.current.** in julia-tests/main.command.tree.wildcard-current.test.jl preserve their exact current tree output.
A failing baseline demonstrates the hierarchy-depth gap; it does not prove a fix or satisfy final acceptance.

observations: recur tree robo -d C:/src/kicad_ra --depth 1 dumped all 120+ full leaf hierarchy branches down to 6+ dotted segments because --depth limits WalkDir filesystem directory depth (docs/, scripts/, warps/ are all directory depth 1) while --help ambiguously said 'Maximum depth to display'.

julia-tests/runtests.tree.jl lines 52-53 already recorded '@test_broken !contains(output, "Create")' noting that --depth 1 did not limit hierarchy depth, while tests/tree_configured_lanes.rs line 232 explicitly depends on --depth 2 limiting filesystem directory walk depth.
recur tree '**' -d C:/src/kicad_ra exited 2 (No files found matching base pattern '**') instead of discovering top-level prefixes or pointing the caller to recur init --analyze / prefix patterns.

final_state.description: Callers can request compact top-level hierarchy summaries beneath any base prefix using recur tree <BASE> --levels <N> (or --tree-depth <N>) in text, --count, and --json modes while existing --depth filesystem walk callers and tests remain 100% compatible.
required_observations: recur tree <BASE> --levels 1 (and --tree-depth 1) bounds rendered hierarchy children to 1 segment beneath <BASE> in unicode, --ascii, --count, and --json modes, with optional folded child/file counts or clean pruned children.
Omitting --levels / --tree-depth leaves all existing recur tree outputs and JSON schemas unchanged.
recur tree --help explicitly distinguishes --depth (filesystem directory traversal depth) from --levels / --tree-depth (dot/separator hierarchy segment depth beneath <BASE>).

Bare wildcard root queries such as recur tree '**' emit an actionable hint naming recur init --analyze or concrete <BASE> prefixes rather than a bare 'No files found' dead end, without altering non-bare wildcard queries like 'main.**.current.**'.
tests/tree_configured_lanes.rs, julia-tests/runtests.tree.jl, and julia-tests/main.command.tree.wildcard-current.test.jl pass without regression.
